config.title: Designing for failure

intro.title: Designing for failure
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple, resilient web service that simulates handling a failure scenario, such as a database connection error. You will learn the core concept of graceful degradation, which ensures your system continues to function partially when a component fails. The main technologies involved include using error handling constructs like try-catch blocks and fallback mechanisms. By the end, you'll understand how to design systems that remain operational and provide a better user experience even when things go wrong.
intro.usecase: Designing for failure is essential in systems where reliability directly impacts user experience and business outcomes. In e-commerce platforms, this appears as graceful handling of payment gateway failures with fallback payment methods and clear error messages. Streaming services implement it through automatic quality degradation when network conditions worsen, ensuring uninterrupted playback. Cloud-based applications use circuit breakers in microservices to prevent cascading failures when dependent services become unavailable. These patterns ensure systems remain functional and user-friendly even when components fail.

objectives: Implement a circuit breaker pattern to prevent cascading failures
Configure retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures
Construct a fallback mechanism to maintain partial functionality during outages
Apply health check endpoints to monitor system component availability
Initialize a bulkhead pattern to isolate failures within system boundaries
Integrate timeout controls to prevent resource exhaustion from hanging requests
Manipulate load balancer configurations to route traffic away from failing nodes

steps.title: Define the core concepts of designing for failure
steps.instruction: Create a function named designForFailurePrinciples that returns a string describing the three key principles: redundancy, graceful degradation, and monitoring.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a string explaining these concepts. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function is defined that returns a string containing the three key principles.
successCriteria: The function designForFailurePrinciples exists and returns a string mentioning redundancy, graceful degradation, and monitoring.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it returns a string that explicitly mentions all three principles: redundancy, graceful degradation, and monitoring.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named designForFailurePrinciples that returns a string describing redundancy, graceful degradation, and monitoring.

steps.title: Identify common failure points in a system
steps.instruction: Inside your designForFailurePrinciples function, create an array named 'commonFailurePoints' that lists these four failure points as strings: 'network latency', 'database outages', 'third-party API failures', and 'hardware faults'.
steps.hint: You can define an array using square brackets with string elements separated by commas.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an array of concepts
const designPrinciples = ['redundancy', 'monitoring', 'graceful degradation'];
steps.expectedOutcome: Your function will contain an array with the four specified failure points as strings.
successCriteria: The function contains an array named 'commonFailurePoints' with exactly four string elements matching the specified failure points.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created an array, but check that it contains all four specified failure points as strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The array is missing or doesn't match the required failure points. Try creating an array with the four specified strings.

steps.title: Design a redundant component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named RedundantComponent that returns a simple div element with the text 'Primary Instance' inside.
steps.hint: Define a component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax that returns JSX containing a div with the specified text.
steps.expectedOutcome: A RedundantComponent function is defined that returns a div element containing 'Primary Instance' text.
successCriteria: The RedundantComponent is defined and returns a div element with the text 'Primary Instance'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it's named exactly 'RedundantComponent' and returns a div with the text 'Primary Instance'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Create a function named RedundantComponent that returns a div element containing 'Primary Instance'.

steps.title: Implement graceful degradation
steps.instruction: Create a function named gracefulDegradation that returns a fallback message when a feature fails.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a string describing the fallback behavior.
steps.expectedOutcome: A gracefulDegradation function is defined that returns a fallback message string.
successCriteria: The gracefulDegradation function is created and returns a string describing fallback functionality.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it returns a string describing fallback behavior.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gracefulDegradation function is not properly defined or doesn't return a fallback message.

steps.title: Add monitoring and alerting
steps.instruction: Create a function named monitorComponent that defines two metrics (errorRate and latency) and returns an object with thresholds that trigger alerts when exceeded.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object containing metric thresholds. You can set numeric values for errorRate and latency thresholds.
steps.expectedOutcome: A monitorComponent function that returns an object with errorRate and latency thresholds to enable alerting.
successCriteria: The monitorComponent function is defined and returns an object containing errorRate and latency threshold values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function returns an object with both errorRate and latency thresholds.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Create a function named monitorComponent that returns an object with errorRate and latency threshold properties.

steps.title: Design a retry mechanism
steps.instruction: Create a function named retryWithExponentialBackoff that implements an exponential backoff strategy for retrying failed operations.
steps.hint: The function should take parameters like the operation to retry, maximum retries, and initial delay. Inside, use a loop or recursion to attempt the operation, increasing the delay exponentially after each failure.
steps.expectedOutcome: A retryWithExponentialBackoff function is added to the code, implementing exponential backoff logic to handle transient failures.
successCriteria: The retryWithExponentialBackoff function is defined with parameters for the operation, maximum retries, and initial delay, and includes exponential delay increase logic.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the retry function, but make sure it includes exponential delay increase (e.g., doubling the delay each retry) and handles the maximum retry limit.
steps.feedbackWrong: The retry mechanism is missing or incorrect. Review exponential backoff patterns: the delay should increase exponentially (e.g., multiply by 2) after each failure, with a maximum retry limit.

steps.title: Implement circuit breaker pattern
steps.instruction: Create a function named circuitBreaker that tracks failures and opens after a threshold is reached, preventing further requests to a failing service.
steps.hint: Think of the circuit breaker as a safety switch that stops requests when a service is failing too often.
steps.expectedOutcome: A circuitBreaker function is defined that will help prevent cascading failures by stopping requests to failing services.
successCriteria: The circuitBreaker function is created with a name that matches the instruction.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you create a function named circuitBreaker that tracks failures and opens after a threshold.
steps.feedbackWrong: The circuit breaker pattern wasn't implemented correctly. Review the concept of preventing cascading failures by stopping requests to failing services.

steps.title: Create a load balancer design
steps.instruction: Create a function named loadBalancer that distributes traffic to healthy instances and removes failed ones.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes an array of instances and returns the selected healthy instance.
steps.expectedOutcome: A loadBalancer function is created that implements basic load balancing logic.
successCriteria: The loadBalancer function is defined and includes logic to select from healthy instances.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the load balancer function. Make sure it includes logic to filter healthy instances and select one.
steps.feedbackWrong: The load balancer function isn't properly implemented. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Design data replication strategy
steps.instruction: Create a function named dataReplicationStrategy that returns a string describing a multi-region replication approach.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a descriptive string about how data is replicated across geographic regions.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that defines a data replication strategy for ensuring availability during failures.
successCriteria: The dataReplicationStrategy function is defined and returns a string describing multi-region replication.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the function, but make sure it returns a descriptive string about multi-region replication.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named dataReplicationStrategy that returns a string describing the replication approach.

steps.title: Combine all patterns into a complete system design
steps.instruction: Create a function named completeSystemDesign that returns a string describing how all the previously defined patterns work together in a robust system.
steps.hint: Write a function that returns a descriptive string about integrating redundancy, circuit breakers, monitoring, graceful degradation, retry mechanisms, load balancing, and data replication.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named completeSystemDesign that returns a string describing the integration of all failure-handling patterns.
successCriteria: The completeSystemDesign function exists and returns a string that mentions at least three of the patterns (e.g., redundancy, circuit breakers, monitoring).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the function, but make sure it returns a descriptive string that mentions how different patterns integrate.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't return a string describing the integration of patterns. Try creating a function named completeSystemDesign that returns a descriptive string.
